findings.text: _stdout_has_reader answers True for every descriptor that is neither regular nor a FIFO, so a terminal and /dev/null both count as 'a reader'. /dev/null has no reader at all, and session_host.py:376 launches followers with no --lifetime (its module docstring, lines 11-13, says the follower's stdout is the host's), so a follower that outlives a dead owner with such a stdout never ends, keeps the session's registration and refuses every dispatch from that session watcher-required - the outcome _check_consumer's docstring at :1727 says this branch preserves. The sibling guards arm the follower with a regular-file stdout (test_orphaned_follower_releases.py:73-89, test_follower_checks_its_owner.py:_STUB), so no test covers the char-device branch.

the _check_consumer docstring still states 'An arming whose output goes to a file or a terminal keeps the owner-only rule', which is the opposite of what the code does since c7de78b608: _stdout_has_reader returns True for any non-FIFO descriptor, terminals included. The function's own docstring says terminals answer yes, so the two docstrings in the same change contradict each other and the safety rationale a reader relies on is the false one.

delivery_mode (and _descriptor_kind at :161 with DELIVERING_MODES) already classify what consumes a process's stdout, and _trace_delivery at :173 already follows a pipe to the pids on its read end with a TTL'd cache. _stdout_has_reader adds a second classifier of the same capability rather than extending that owner: it re-implements the kind rule with stat.S_ISREG/stat.S_ISFIFO and re-derives its own reader answer, and it reaches into the owner only for the private _pipe_reader_pids (:137). It does not extend the owner; it duplicates its classification with a deliberately different policy (any process holding the read end rather than the end of the chain).

negative_control_log carries a path plus a quoted description and two further paths on one line, so it is not the bare path the manifest contract requires. `reckon crew check --manifest --run r-20261114T101135327049-follower-outlives-arming-shell-s134` refuses on it: "negative_control_log 'scratch/negative-control.log (owner-only check restored: 1 failed); also scratch/negative-control-base.log and scratch/negative-control-repair.log' does not resolve to a readable log file". The red log exists at scratch/negative-control.log (1 failed, EXIT=1), so the repair is to name that path alone.

the fragment cites the ruff result as a done-when receipt, but the only ruff log (scratch/ruff-head.log) is headed 'ee25b58b3cd5 + repair working tree', so it predates the final source change in c7de78b608 and is not a head-revision receipt. Re-running ruff check on the head files confirms the claim itself: 2 findings, SIM103 at reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:98 and SIM115, both outside the introduced block and both present at base.

the recorded observation that 'in both cases of the new test the owner/reader probe is never called' is not supportable and understates the coverage it claims to lack: the negative control at scratch/negative-control.log restores the owner-only branch and reddens the first case, which can only differ from the head at the _stdout_has_reader call (:1750), so that call is reached in both arms of that comparison.
